line: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 Aura Edition (2026, Panther Lake)
config_name: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 — Core Ultra 7 356H, 32GB LPDDR5, 512GB SSD, 14" 2.8K 120Hz matte OLED

specs.keyboard_notes: ThinkPad keyboard 1.5mm travel, TrackPoint, haptic touchpad option

battery.notes: 58Wh. CNET: battery life shorter than Gen 13; ~9-10h light mixed use on OLED.

price.notes: CNET listed US$2,374 as-tested; Lenovo CA runs heavy e-coupons. CAD estimate from US price x ~1.3 with CA pricing often closer to parity during promos.

reviews.quote: The X1 Carbon Gen 14 introduces Lenovo's Space Frame chassis that features a smaller motherboard and larger cooling fans, along with a modular design that makes it easier to access and then repair or replace individual components.
This year's model isn't any faster than last year's ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 13, and battery life is actually a few hours shorter.

the X1 Carbon is lighter than MacBooks, starting at 1 kilo for the OLED variant... the X1 Carbon is a more ergonomic chassis, with friendlier edges, a screen that opens flat to 180 degrees, and better IO

praises: Space Frame redesign means the SSD, battery and ports are genuinely swappable now — first X1 owners can actually keep the machine past warranty
Free OLED upgrade at Lenovo right now: matte 2.8K 120Hz panel with no visible PWM flicker at 120Hz
Still the lightest 14-inch business flagship at ~1.0 kg — disappears in a backpack
Best-in-class ThinkPad keyboard plus TrackPoint; haptic touchpad is a real improvement over Gen 13
Dual-fan cooling runs whisper-quiet in Balanced mode even with 40 Chrome tabs open
complaints: Battery is a regression vs Gen 13 — Lunar Lake model lasted noticeably longer in CNET's testing
No performance uplift over Gen 13; Core Ultra 300 series is roughly a wash with Lunar Lake in office work
Config pricing at checkout balloons fast; the 'sale' price assumes stacking eCoupon codes
Speakers are mediocre bottom-firing units — thin on calls compared to OmniBook/Dell quad-speaker rivals
Only 32GB max RAM and it is soldered — road warriors wanting 64GB are out of luck

design_philosophy: Lenovo's flagship business ultraportable: carbon-fiber/magnesium chassis, classic black ThinkPad DNA, maximum lightness with full portage. The Gen 14's Space Frame re-engineering prioritises repairability and cooling over raw speed, targeting corporate fleets and road warriors who keep machines 3-5 years.
rating_notes: Ratings anchored on CNET's reviewed Gen 14 config (OLED tier, US$2,374) plus Ultrabookreview's Gen 14 review; matte OLED gives readability_dark 9 (no bleed, low min brightness). 512GB base storage is the only delta vs reviewed config (storage downgrade −0.5 upgradability-neutral).
